newsitem.title: MEXICO: PEMEX SEES $240 MLN INVESTMENT IN REFINERY.
newsitem.headline: PEMEX SEES $240 MLN INVESTMENT IN REFINERY.

text.p: Mexico's oil monopoly Petroleos Mexicanos (Pemex) plans to invest $240 million in a project to boost crude processing capacity at its smallest refinery, a company spokesman said on Tuesday.
With four new plants at the Ciudad Madero refinery, Pemex aims to increase the refinery's crude processing capacity by 40,000 barrels per day (bpd) for a total 205,000 bpd, he said.
"It includes a hydrodesulfurization plant, an isomerization plant, a hexane-pentane plant and a water recycling plant," refinery spokesman Faruk Fayad Zellek told Reuters.
Construction is expected to be completed by the end of 1998, with preliminary studies currently in place, he said.

Fayad said the new plants will help make up for a lag in unleaded gasoline production, and also produce jet fuel and fuel oil. The refined products are distributed to Tamaulipas, Coahuila, San Luis Potosi and Nuevo Leon states in Northern Mexico.
Companies that won the contracts to build the new plants include Protexa and Cydsa, he said.
The new processing capacity should help Mexico use an increasing supply of heavy crude Maya and possibly cut down on Mexico's about 75,000 bpd gasoline imports seen for the year.
